title: VAPT Platform Scope & Enforcement Contract v3.0
description: Machine-readable contract governing the VAPT WordPress Plugin Builder's platform scope, enforcer constraints, and compliance validation rules. This contract is loaded by the AI Agent at runtime and enforced as a hard constraint on all generation, validation, and diagnostic tasks. It replaces informal scope definitions and serves as the single source of truth for platform compliance.

stakeholder_context.objective: Build WordPress plugins that provide security against VAPT risks and harden WordPress installations following OWASP's latest recommendations
stakeholder_context.environment_constraint: Strictly WordPress — all enforcement must be achievable within a WordPress plugin context on standard and shared hosting
stakeholder_context.target_audience: WordPress site owners on Apache, LiteSpeed, Nginx, and CloudFlare infrastructure

allowed_platforms.name: Apache HTTP Server
allowed_platforms.notes: Primary enforcer via .htaccess; server-level directives via apache enforcer. LiteSpeed shares .htaccess compatibility.

allowed_platforms.name: LiteSpeed Web Server
allowed_platforms.notes: LiteSpeed natively supports .htaccess rules. Dedicated litespeed enforcer key added for LiteSpeed-specific optimizations (e.g., CacheLookup, RewriteEngine LiteSpeed-specific directives). Existing htaccess rules serve as the baseline — litespeed key adds server-specific enhancements where applicable.

allowed_platforms.name: Nginx Web Server
allowed_platforms.notes: Requires server-level access for configuration. Rate limiting via limit_req_zone.

allowed_platforms.name: CloudFlare CDN/WAF
allowed_platforms.notes: Derived from htaccess rules. Includes transform_rule, waf_custom_rule, and notes_only implementation types. Rate limiting beyond simple thresholds requires CloudFlare Pro or higher.

prohibited_platforms.name: Microsoft IIS
prohibited_platforms.reason: Not in target infrastructure. IIS web.config rules are irrelevant to WordPress on Apache/LiteSpeed/Nginx/CloudFlare environments.

prohibited_platforms.name: Caddy Web Server
prohibited_platforms.reason: Not in target infrastructure. Caddyfile v2 rules are irrelevant to the target WordPress hosting environments.

prohibited_platforms.name: fail2ban Intrusion Prevention
prohibited_platforms.reason: Requires server-level filesystem access (/etc/fail2ban/jail.local) which a WordPress plugin cannot write to on standard or shared hosting. Incompatible with the WordPress plugin execution context. Replaced by PHP rate limiting (transient-based), CloudFlare WAF rules, Nginx limit_req_zone, and Apache mod_ratelimit.

replacement_strategy.php_functions: WordPress transient-based rate limiting using get_transient/set_transient — already exists for most risks as php_functions enforcer
replacement_strategy.cloudflare: CloudFlare WAF Custom Rules and Rate Limiting rules — already exists as cloudflare enforcer
replacement_strategy.nginx: Nginx limit_req_zone and limit_req directives — to be added where applicable
replacement_strategy.apache: Apache mod_ratelimit or mod_evasive directives — to be added where applicable

risk_deletions.reason: Caddy-native risk. A find-and-replace error corrupted this entry by replacing 'Caddy' with 'Apache_Legacy', breaking all references (/etc/Apache_Legacy/Caddyfile is not a real path, Apache_Legacy validate is not a real command). Since Caddy is a prohibited platform, deletion is the correct remediation — do NOT attempt to restore.
Caddy-native risk. Same Apache_Legacy corruption as RISK-123. Since Caddy is a prohibited platform, deletion is the correct remediation.

corruption_fixes.description: Apache_Legacy corruption — a find-and-replace error replaced 'Caddy' with 'Apache_Legacy' across enforcer_pattern_library_v2.0.json, vapt_driver_manifest_v2.0.json, and interface_schema_v2.0.json. This affected the description field, enforcer_key_map, and RISK-123/RISK-124 entries.
corruption_fixes.resolution: Since RISK-123 and RISK-124 are being deleted (Caddy-native), the corruption in those entries is resolved by deletion. Remaining 'Apache_Legacy' references in enforcer_key_map and description fields are corrected to their proper values or removed.
affected_fields: enforcer_pattern_library_v2.0.json / enforcer_key_map.htaccess — remove 'Apache_Legacy' from derivation list
enforcer_pattern_library_v2.0.json / enforcer_key_map.caddy_native — restore to 'Native Caddy enforcer risks (RISK-123, RISK-124) — DELETED in v3.0' or remove

litespeed_integration.strategy: LiteSpeed natively supports .htaccess directives, so existing Apache htaccess rules work without modification. The litespeed enforcer key is added as a supplementary enforcer for risks where LiteSpeed-specific optimizations provide additional security value.
litespeed_integration.marker_style: same as htaccess (# BEGIN VAPT / # END Of)

applicable_risks.directive:
<IfModule LiteSpeed>
    Header unset Server
    Header always unset X-Powered-By
</IfModule>
applicable_risks.note: LiteSpeed-specific header suppression using IfModule LiteSpeed wrapper
LiteSpeed respects Options -Indexes identically to Apache — existing htaccess rule is sufficient, litespeed key references the same

applicable_risks.directive:
<FilesMatch "\.(php|phtml)$">
    <IfModule LiteSpeed>
        Order Deny,Allow
        Deny from all
    </IfModule>
</FilesMatch>
applicable_risks.note: LiteSpeed-specific PHP execution blocking in uploads directory

applicable_risks.directive:
<IfModule LiteSpeed>
    Header unset Server
    ServerSignature Off
</IfModule>

applicable_risks.note: LiteSpeed version hiding via header removal

cross_platform_notes.htaccess_compatibility: All existing htaccess rules work on LiteSpeed without modification. The litespeed key provides supplementary directives only where LiteSpeed-specific optimizations add value beyond the Apache baseline.
cross_platform_notes.no_separate_config: Unlike Nginx, LiteSpeed does not require a separate configuration file — it reads .htaccess natively.
cross_platform_notes.lscache: LiteSpeed Cache plugin integration is out of scope for VAPT hardening but should be noted as a compatibility consideration.

structural_preservation_rule.description: The JSON schema/structure of all 6 existing bundle files is IMMUTABLE. Remediation may only add or remove key-value pairs within the existing structure — never change the structure itself.
rules: Top-level keys (schema_version, bundle_files, patterns, risks, risk_interfaces, etc.) must NEVER be renamed, removed, or reordered
The nesting hierarchy must remain identical — if htaccess is a sibling of nginx inside a risk object, litespeed must be added as the same type of sibling
Value types must be preserved — strings stay strings, objects stay objects, arrays stay arrays
New enforcer entries (litespeed) must follow the exact same key structure as existing siblings (nginx, apache, etc.)
Removed entries delete only their own key from the parent object — the parent object and its other keys remain untouched
The contract file (vapt_platform_contract_v3.0.json) is a NEW file with its own independent structure and is not bound by this rule
JSON formatting style (indentation, key ordering conventions) should match the source files

gate_1_platform_scope.description: No generated code or UI schema may reference a prohibited platform
gate_1_platform_scope.check: For every platform_implementations entry in interface_schema, verify platform is in allowed_platforms[]

gate_2_enforcer_keys.description: No enforcer pattern may use a prohibited enforcer key (fail2ban, caddy_native, caddy, iis)
gate_2_enforcer_keys.check: For every lib_key in enforcer_pattern_library patterns, verify key is in allowed enforcer keys list

gate_3_risk_existence.description: Deleted risks (RISK-123, RISK-124) must not appear in any bundle file
gate_3_risk_existence.check: Verify RISK-123 and RISK-124 do not exist as keys in any patterns, risks, or risk_interfaces object

gate_4_litespeed_presence.description: LiteSpeed must be represented as a platform in at least the key risks where it provides supplementary value
gate_4_litespeed_presence.check: Verify litespeed enforcer key exists in enforcer_pattern_library for at least the applicable_risks listed above

gate_5_apache_legacy_corruption.description: No 'Apache_Legacy' string may appear in any bundle file — this indicates unresolved corruption
gate_5_apache_legacy_corruption.check: Grep all bundle files for 'Apache_Legacy' — must return zero results

gate_6_cross_reference_integrity.description: Every code_ref and driver_ref in interface_schema must resolve to an existing entry in the pattern library and driver manifest respectively
gate_6_cross_reference_integrity.check: For each risk_interface, verify code_ref points to existing lib_key in pattern library and driver_ref resolves to existing step in manifest

gate_7_wordpress_context.description: All enforcement must be achievable within a WordPress plugin context — no server-level filesystem writes outside ABSPATH or standard WordPress plugin paths, except for Nginx and Apache server config files which require server admin access
gate_7_wordpress_context.check: Verify all target_file paths either contain {ABSPATH} or are documented server-level paths (/etc/nginx/*, /etc/apache2/*)

self_check_rubric_updates.description: The AI Agent self-check rubric in ai_agent_instructions_v2.0.json must be updated to reflect the contract constraints

removed_checks.old_text: IIS <rewrite> sections include URL Rewrite Module 2.1 requirement note
removed_checks.action: REPLACE with platform scope validation check

removed_checks.old_text: Caddy output uses v2 syntax only — no Apache directives, no semicolons, no Order/Deny

new_checks.check: All platforms in output are within contract.allowed_platforms — no IIS, Caddy, or fail2ban references generated
LiteSpeed enforcer key present for risks where litespeed-specific directives add value — htaccess rules marked as LiteSpeed-compatible

self_check_rubric_updates.scoring_rule: Sum weights of passing checks. Score < 18 → identify failing checks and regenerate. Contract gates 1, 2, 3, 5 are CRITICAL — any violation blocks delivery regardless of total score.

remediation_execution_log.description: Tracks the remediation actions taken to bring all 6 bundle files into compliance with this contract

contract_enforcement.agent_instruction_append: BEFORE generating any output, load vapt_platform_contract_v3.0.json and validate ALL contract_validation_gates pass. If any CRITICAL gate fails, block delivery and report the violation. This contract supersedes any platform references in ai_agent_instructions_v2.0.json that conflict with it.
contract_enforcement.runtime_validation: On every generate_full_risk_package or generate_enforcement_code task, the agent MUST: (1) verify the requested platform is in contract.platform_scope.allowed_platforms[], (2) verify the enforcer_key is NOT in contract.contract_validation_gates.gate_2_enforcer_keys.prohibited_enforcer_keys[], (3) verify the risk_id is NOT in contract.risk_deletions[].risk_id. If any check fails, refuse the generation and report the contract violation.
